label: rem:springer-fibre-convention-scope
title: Prior art: Springer's correspondence and the convention behind the sign of $\Delta_\lambda$
html:
For G = GL_n and a unipotent element x with Springer fibre \mathcal{B}_x of dimension d_x, Springer's theorem identifies the top cohomology H^{2d_x}(\mathcal{B}_x) with an irreducible representation V_\lambda of S_n, where \lambda is the Jordan type of x, under the normalisation in which V_{(n)} is the trivial and V_{(1^n)} the sign representation [shoji2019, Thm 2.1 and eq. (2.1), \S 2, pp. 3--4]. The same survey uses the statistic n(\lambda) = \sum_i (i-1)\lambda_i [shoji2019, eq. (6.3), \S 6], which is the grade n(\lambda) of the unification proposition.

What this gives here. The two factors of \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)} \dim V_\lambda behave differently under the choice of convention:

  • the magnitude is convention-free, since \dim V_\lambda = \dim V_{\lambda'};
  • the sign depends on whether \lambda or its conjugate \lambda' labels V_\lambda, because n(\lambda) \neq n(\lambda') in general.

Under Shoji's normalisation the sign is the parity of the Springer-fibre dimension, (-1)^{n(\lambda)} = (-1)^{d_x} for x of Jordan type \lambda. This is checked at the two ends of the dominance order. For \lambda = (n), x is regular, \mathcal{B}_x is a point, n(\lambda) = 0, and the representation is trivial. For \lambda = (1^n), x = 1, \mathcal{B}_x is the whole flag variety of dimension n(n-1)/2 = n(1^n), and the representation is the sign. The general equality d_x = n(\lambda) is standard, but the survey cited does not state it, so it is not attributed to that source here.

What it does not supply. The proof of the unification proposition does not use this citation; the Springer reading is an interpretation of its sign, not an input to its proof. It also does not bear on the many-body binding magnitude, which that proposition leaves open.
